findings: Schema re-run failure — ALTER statements for column renames (sp_rename) and type changes (ALTER COLUMN) lack IF NOT EXISTS guards. Running COMPLETE_SCHEMA_FIX.sql twice will fail. Add column existence checks before sp_rename and ALTER COLUMN, or document that the script requires a fresh database.

Destructive Schedules migration — Schedules date/time transformation drops ScheduledDate, StartTime (TIME), EndTime (TIME) and replaces with StartTime/EndTime (DATETIME2). If the TIME-type columns already exist, the migration runs; if they're already DATETIME2, it skips. But the dropped columns are gone forever. Document this as a breaking change or add a rollback script.

Invoice MemberId defaults to 0 in seed data — COMPLETE_SEED_DATA.sql creates Users with Role='SuperAdmin' and Role='Trainer' but no MemberId (defaults to NULL or 0). If any invoice creation logic reads from Users.MemberId, it will write 0 to Invoices.MemberId, causing FK violations or orphaned invoices. The seed script avoids this by inserting Invoices directly from Memberships, but the Users table seeding should either set MemberId explicitly or document that non-Member users have NULL MemberId.

Payments.MemberId defaults to 0 in schema — COMPLETE_SCHEMA_FIX.sql adds Payments.MemberId with DEFAULT 0. If existing Payments rows exist, they'll get MemberId=0, violating the FK to Members (no Member with MemberId=0). Change DEFAULT to NULL and make the column nullable, or add a migration step to backfill MemberId from Invoices.MemberId before adding the FK constraint.

Cancellation success on wrong member — MembershipService.CancelAsync checks entity.MemberId != requestingMemberId and returns false. The controller for Admin/SuperAdmin calls CancelAsync with membership.MemberId (the owner's ID), so the service check passes. The controller for Member calls it with userMemberId. Both paths work, but the service method's requestingMemberId parameter is misleading for the admin path. Rename parameter to ownerMemberId or remove the check from the service layer and enforce it only in the controller.

Seed script Trainer FK gap — COMPLETE_SEED_DATA.sql inserts 5 Trainers with auto-increment TrainerId (1-5), then inserts 5 Trainer Users. But the Users table has no TrainerId FK column, so the link is by email and FullName only (string matching). If a trainer's email changes, the link breaks. Add a TrainerId column to Users or document that Trainer users are matched by email, not by FK.

Sessions seed data hardcoded range — COMPLETE_SEED_DATA.sql seeds Sessions for ScheduleId 1-60, but only if 240 schedules exist. The seed script creates 240 schedules (30 days × 8), so ScheduleId should go up to 240. Seeding only 1-60 leaves the remaining 180 schedules with no registrations. Change the loop to cover all 240 or document why only the first 60 are seeded.
